title: Singular Hodge Atoms at Conifold Degenerations: Recollement, Rees Non-Splitting, Exceptional-Curve Relations, and Hecke Costalk Detection
content: We define a marked singular conifold Hodge atom as the extension-bearing mixed-Hodge-module datum comprising the intersection-complex constituent, the (-2)-twisted punctual quotient, and their specified attaching morphism. The construction uses open--closed recollement rather than spectral decomposition; it is not an identification with a Katzarkov–Kontsevich–Pantev–Yu spectral atom. For the determinantal ordinary double point, a filtered localization model proves that the canonical and every nonzero corrected local attachment remain nonsplit after associated-graded Rees specialization. When a projective small resolution with smooth source exists, codimension-two purity and the Gysin map identify the rational global attaching boundary with the signed exceptional-curve class map, up to the marked diagonal rescaling. For successive framed rank-two Hecke modifications, we compute the complete scheme-theoretic punctual first-jet incidence, its reduced mixed Hodge cohomology and terminal-lattice images, and establish naturality of the transported extension under the specified two-step composition equivalence. An extraordinary-costalk theorem proves nonvanishing under explicit properness, smooth-purity, node-factorization, and constant-kernel hypotheses; their verification on the genuine Higgs charts and the numerical perverse boundary maps remain open. A synthesis theorem collects these separately scoped results. Finally, an exact filtered-flat Rees functor produces formal F-bundles without asserting an unconstructed singular-to-quantum comparison.
